name: Mast Room
summary: In the Deadmines, timber from Westfall reaches the Mast Room, where goblin woodcarvers shape it for the Defias.

sections.title: The Underground Sawmill
sections.body: Deep in the Deadmines, the Mast Room turns timber from Westfall into parts for a warship. Felled logs, sawdust, and great cutting machines fill the cavern. Goblin woodcarvers shape the masts, ribs, and planks for the vessel hidden farther within Ironclad Cove. Sneed watches over their work as the Defias Brotherhood puts the timber to war.

sections.title: Industrial Labor
sections.body: From atop a mechanical shredder, Sneed directs the goblin woodcarvers. Logs rise and pass through the planers in a steady flow, while the workers meet his demanding quotas. The old gold mine rings with the labor of a shipyard, where timber becomes the pieces of a vessel.

faq.q: Why is there a lumber mill inside an underground mine?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood is secretly building a great warship in the cove beneath the mines. In the Mast Room, timber smuggled from Westfall becomes its masts, framing, and hull planks.
Sneed runs the Mast Room and directs goblin woodcarvers from atop a lethal mechanical lumber shredder.

faq.q: Why are goblins working here for the Defias?
faq.answer: Edwin VanCleef hired goblin engineers and craftsmen for expertise human stonemasons lacked. For gold and profit, the goblins bring heavy machinery, explosives, and shipwright skills.

angles.text: Sneed's goblin shredder uses crude steam-and-cog machinery, adapted from forest logging to crush intruders.
Timber from this chamber shows that Defias pillaging across Westfall serves a coordinated industrial effort.
